claims.text: The target material is an AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy.
Grain boundary engineering can improve the toughness of AlCoCrFeNi.
Grain boundary engineering promotes favorable grain boundary characters.
Grain boundary engineering promotes grain boundary segregation.
Favorable grain boundary characters lead to improved deformation mechanisms.
Grain boundary segregation leads to improved deformation mechanisms.
The improved deformation mechanisms increase toughness.
At lower temperatures within the stated range, the grain-boundary-engineered alloy will be tougher than the untreated baseline.
At higher temperatures within the stated range, the alloy will exhibit reduced toughness.
Higher-temperature exposure causes grain boundary coarsening.
Higher-temperature exposure causes loss of grain boundary segregation.
Grain boundary coarsening and loss of segregation cause the predicted reduction in toughness at higher temperatures.
The proposed behavior is applicable under uniaxial tensile loading from -20 °C to 200 °C.
The effect of grain boundary engineering on toughness across the stated temperature range is not well established.
The proposed test conditions may not represent typical engineering service.

contradictions.description: The prediction allows reduced toughness at higher temperatures, but the falsification rule states without a temperature qualification that any failure to improve toughness falsifies the hypothesis. Thus, the predicted high-temperature result could itself trigger the stated falsification rule.
